problem_type: A multi-step model-facing contract designed for a code caller and handed to a language model: the published schema, the error vocabulary, the lifecycle vocabulary and the handle format each carry information the model cannot act on, so the flow is unwalkable without a human writing every argument by hand
symptom: An external AI host driving Nomi's MCP model-onboarding surface (measured 2026-09-10 with Codex CLI 0.153.4 against a real DeepSeek key) got arguments right on only 36 of 58 calls (62%) and completed only 1 of 9 agent turns, and that one turn only after every argument was dictated to it. The spend-confirmation step was structurally unwalkable: the GUI showed nothing while a verification handoff sat in the queue, the agent could not tell 'waiting for the person' from 'the person approved', and a repeated confirm invalidated the click the person had just made (3 of 4 clicks were wasted).
direct_cause: Six independent surfaces each hid a fact the model needed. (1) integrationSession.requestConfirmation minted a fresh challenge on every call and stage stayed needs_spend_confirmation before and after the human gesture, so a second confirm replaced pendingChallengeId and voided the pending click; no renderer outside SettingsDialog listened to the verification handoff. (2) approvalReceipt.mintReceipt set the receipt expiresAt to challenge.expiresAt, so the 5-minute window covered 'human notices and clicks' and 'agent spends it' together. (3) dispatcher project.list/project.create returned the 1271-character signed selection token as projectSelectionHandle and projectSessionAuthority.open accepted only that token. (4) MCP_INTEGRATION_TOOL advertised required: ['action'] while integrationSession threw on kind/name/baseUrl/expectedRevision/idempotencyKey one field at a time. (5) mutate/requestConfirmation/start/cancel all threw the same bare English 'Integration session revision is stale' for a missing field, a behind value, an invented value and a concurrent write. (6) integration.get demanded a sessionId and begin created a new session even when one already existed for the same owner and base URL, so a lost session id had no route home and a stored key was asked for twice.
class_root: Nomi published a machine contract without keeping it honest about itself. Each of the six surfaces answers a question the caller must answer to take the next step - what is required, what went wrong, whose turn it is, which handle to send, which session am I in - and in each case the published answer was either absent, ambiguous, or contradicted by the implementation. The missing invariant is: every fact a caller needs to take the next step must be published in the contract the caller can read, and must be the same fact the implementation enforces.
affected_population: Every external MCP host driving model onboarding (Codex CLI, Claude Code, Cursor and any future registered client) - the surface is identical for all of them
Every user who asks an external AI to connect a model for them, which is the whole point of the MCP onboarding surface
Every Nomi-owned in-app onboarding session, which shares the same IntegrationSessionService lifecycle and the same approval receipt authority
Every caller of the project selection handle, because project.list and project.create both issued the oversized token
entry_points: MCP tools/call nomi_integration (begin / open_credentials / propose / confirm / start / cancel) from any registered external host
MCP tools/call nomi_read target=integration, with and without a sessionId
MCP tools/call nomi_session_open with a projectSelectionHandle from nomi_read target=projects or nomi_project_create
The trusted Nomi UI confirmation path nomi:integration-session:confirm (IntegrationConfirmationPanel)
The capability-core RPC dispatcher used by the in-app onboarding drawer, which shares every integration.* case with the MCP transport

external_sources.purpose: Defines inputSchema as plain JSON Schema and separates protocol errors (JSON-RPC) from tool execution errors reported with isError: true, which fixes both the shape of the honest required declaration and where the new error codes belong.
Establishes allOf + if/then as the standard expression of conditional required fields, so the per-action required set does not need a private keyword (R31).

Confirms the 2025-06-18 revision has no URL mode and that servers must not request sensitive values through elicitation, so degrading to a human-typed key in Nomi stays correct; only the instruction text needed to say 'wait' instead of implying a retry.
Comparable human-in-the-loop handoff that times the human authorization window and the program's redemption window separately, which is the shape adopted for the challenge TTL versus the receipt TTL.

Establishes that an idempotency key means 'a replay returns the same result', not 'a replay supersedes the previous attempt' - the semantics requestConfirmation now follows so a repeated confirm cannot void a pending human click.

invariants: Every field the implementation requires for an action is named in the contract the model actually receives (the action field's description, generated from the same table the tool layer enforces), and nothing is declared that is not enforced
A spend challenge that has already been issued is returned unchanged until it expires or is consumed; a repeated confirm never mints a replacement while a human click is pending
The session stage distinguishes 'the agent must confirm', 'a person must approve' and 'a person approved', and start is reachable only from the last one
A human approval receipt's lifetime starts when the person acts, never when the agent asked
An opaque authority handle reaches a model only as a short id; the signed token stays in the process that issued it
Each distinct write-precondition failure carries its own code plus the concrete value the caller needs to recover (currentRevision, the missing field names)
An owner can always enumerate its own integration sessions without already knowing a session id
Beginning an integration for a target that already has an unfinished session for the same owner resumes it instead of creating a second one
generality_proof: The six repairs land on the boundaries every caller already funnels through, not on the MCP transport. expectedRevision is validated in exactly one function (assertIntegrationRevision in electron/shared/integrationContract.ts) which every write entry - mutate, saveCredential, requestConfirmation, confirmFromTrustedUi, startConfirmedFromTrustedUi, start, cancel - now calls, so the RPC dispatcher used by the in-app drawer and the MCP transport get identical codes. The stage vocabulary lives in the same shared file and is the only source both main and renderer DTOs derive from, so no surface can invent a fourth spend-gate state. The per-action required set exists once as INTEGRATION_REQUIRED_BY_ACTION and is the source of both the published allOf/if-then and the runtime aggregate check, so the schema cannot drift from the implementation; the published shape stays flat on purpose: check:model-schema proves that a root allOf is silently dropped by the Anthropic adapter and that const is unsupported on Google's OpenAPI 3.0.3 path, so a conditional-required schema would have reproduced this very defect class (a contract the model never actually receives). The truth therefore rides in the action field's description, generated from the same table, and the tool layer refuses a call that does not satisfy it. The receipt lifetime is computed inside the single mintReceipt, so the production run gates and the integration gate share the corrected semantics. The selection handle registry lives inside createProjectLeaseAuthority, the only issuer, and projectSessionAuthority.open is the only consumer, so no caller can still pass a raw token.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: The only expectedRevision judgement in the codebase. Splits the previously conflated failure into integration_expected_revision_missing / integration_revision_stale / integration_revision_ahead and attaches currentRevision so the caller does not have to guess.
The single lifecycle vocabulary. Now carries awaiting_human_confirmation and human_confirmed so 'waiting for a person' and 'a person approved' are different observable states for every consumer.

Owns spend-challenge idempotency: while a challenge is live it is returned unchanged regardless of the idempotency key, so a repeated confirm can never void a pending human click, and only an expired challenge is replaced under the original confirmation key.
Owns the human-approval receipt lifetime for every gate in the app. The receipt TTL now starts at mint time (the human gesture) instead of inheriting the challenge deadline.

The single per-action required set. Both the published JSON Schema conditional required rules and the runtime aggregate check derive from it, so the advertised contract and the enforced contract cannot diverge.

Owns the selection handle format: the signed token is kept in the issuing process and only the short handleId crosses the MCP boundary, mirroring the receipt/challenge id indirection already used by the approval authority.

The single agent-facing error projection. The integration codes join the existing bilingual table and the outcome now carries a details object so recovery values reach the caller instead of being buried in prose.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Both the MCP nomi_read target=integration route and the in-app RPC route reach this one case; it now lists the caller's sessions when no sessionId is supplied, so the 'lost session id' dead end is closed for every transport rather than only for MCP.

The trusted UI confirm path calls confirmFromTrustedUi and then startConfirmedFromTrustedUi; both now go through the same stage transition, so an in-app confirmation produces the same human_confirmed state an external host observes.

The only tool that consumes a projectSelectionHandle; it now documents and accepts the short id, and projectSessionAuthority.open resolves through the registry, so no path still accepts a raw signed token.

The production run spend gates consume receipts minted by the same authority, so they inherit the corrected receipt lifetime; the file itself is unchanged because the invariant lives in mintReceipt, and its existing suite (productionRunApprovalReceipt.test.ts) passes unchanged.

The ratchet proved the first attempt wrong: declaring the per-action required with allOf + if/then + const added 9 new violations, because the Anthropic adapter drops a root allOf and Google's legacy path does not read const - the model would have seen a tool with no schema at all. The published schema therefore stays flat and the required set is declared in the action description that every adapter passes through verbatim.

The single-shot generation gate never uses the integration session lifecycle or the project selection handle; its human approval already runs through elicitation-first confirmation inside one tool call, so there is no agent turn between the human gesture and the spend for the TTL change to matter.

The durable handoff queue already persisted and broadcast the verification entry correctly; the defect was that no renderer outside the settings drawer subscribed to it, so the repair is a new subscriber and the queue itself needs no change.

recurrence.reason: The same class - a published machine contract that omits or contradicts a fact the caller needs - can reappear on any tool the model drives, and it did reappear six independent times on one surface. It is not tied to one vendor, model, host or session: every registered MCP client reads the same catalog, and the in-app RPC dispatcher shares every handler, so a seventh omission would reach all of them at once.
same_class_scan: git grep 'revision is stale' across electron/ found seven throw sites in integrationSession.ts sharing one message for four distinct failures; all seven now call assertIntegrationRevision

git grep 'projectSelectionHandle' across electron/, src/ and tests/ found the issuing sites (dispatcher.ts project.list and project.create), the consuming site (projectSessionAuthority.open) and six test/e2e callers, all migrated to the short id in the same change

Enumerated every action of MCP_INTEGRATION_TOOL against IntegrationSessionService's own argument validation to build INTEGRATION_REQUIRED_BY_ACTION, rather than fixing only the three actions the experiment happened to hit

Checked every consumer of INTEGRATION_STAGES (integrationSession.ts write-stage and terminal sets, validateState, the renderer DTOs and the certification projection) before adding the two stages, and the check:vocabularies gate confirms there is still exactly one owner
Checked every caller of mintReceipt (the integration confirm path and the production run gate path) before changing the receipt lifetime; both want 'the window starts when the person acted'

Reviewed the published inputSchema of every tool in MCP_TOOL_CATALOG against the runtime validator's supported keyword set via the existing mcpArgValidation catalog test, so the honest conditional required could not be advertised without also being enforceable

prevention.invariant: The per-action required set exists exactly once (INTEGRATION_REQUIRED_BY_ACTION) and is the source of both the published action description and the runtime aggregate check, and expectedRevision is judged exactly once (assertIntegrationRevision) for every write entry point.
prevention.failure_mode: A missing required field is refused before any dispatch, with every missing field named at once and the action's full required set attached; a wrong expectedRevision is refused with a code that says which of the three things went wrong and what the current revision is; a start before human approval is refused with the stage that blocks it.
prevention.strategy: Both drifts that produced this class - the advertised contract diverging from the enforced one, and one message standing for several distinct failures - are removed by construction rather than by review: the published description is generated from the required table, and the revision judgement has a single function with one code per outcome. The stage vocabulary lives in the shared contract file that check:vocabularies already guards, so a future parallel definition of the spend gate fails the gate instead of shipping.

invariant_owner_layer.note: 接入会话的生命周期词表、写前置条件判据与错误码从此都归这一层；主进程 service、MCP 工具层、渲染层 DTO 都从它派生。第二处平行定义会被 check:vocabularies 拦下。

legacy_paths.rationale: The oversized signed selection token is no longer emitted by project.list or project.create and projectSessionAuthority.open no longer accepts one, so there is no parallel long-token path left to fall back to. The old single 'revision is stale' throw sites are deleted rather than kept as a fallback message, and start no longer accepts the needs_spend_confirmation stage. Persisted sessions written by earlier versions keep their old stage strings and are still read and confirmable - that is stored data, not a second code path.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No third-party runtime controls any of the six invariants. Ajv already supported if/then/const on draft-07; the change was to the repository's own published keyword allowlist, not to the validator version. The MCP protocol version in use (2025-11-25) already provides everything the repairs rely on.

migration: No stored format changes. Integration session files keep schemaVersion 1 and old sessions parked at needs_spend_confirmation are still accepted by confirmFromTrustedUi, so a session created before this change can still be approved by a person. Approval receipt records are unchanged in shape; only newly minted receipts get the later expiry, and previously minted receipts keep the deadline they were signed with. Project selection handles are per-connection and were never persisted, so nothing on disk refers to the old long token.
residual_risks: The spend-gate stage predicate uses the stage name (isSpendGateStage matches names containing 'confirm'). A future stage whose name happens to contain 'confirm' would silently join the gate; the pinning test in mcpOnboardingDefects.test.ts catches that at the vocabulary level but nothing rejects it at compile time.

The loopback fixture is deterministic and free: it proves the published contract is walkable step by step, but it does not prove a real model will choose those steps. The 62% first-try argument rate can only be re-measured by repeating the real-host experiment, which this change does not automate.

The GUI pending-confirmation notice was verified by unit-level reasoning and the existing handoff subscription, not by a Playwright walkthrough on a packaged build; the visual placement of that toast is unproven.

Receipt lifetime is now up to 5 minutes longer in absolute terms for every gate in the app, including production run gates. The window is still bounded and still single-use, but the exposure after a human gesture is strictly larger than before.

The per-action required set cannot be machine-checked by a JSON Schema validator on the client side, because the constructs that would express it (root allOf, const) are dropped or unsupported by real model adapters. A host that ignores the action description still learns the required set only from the first refusal - one round trip, with every missing field named, instead of one per field.
